macOS pgrep leaves out its own ancestors unless given -a, so molt run inside a Claude Code session did not see that session (claude liberator, ST0006). procps' pgrep leaves out only itself, and its -a lists full command lines, so the flag is macOS-only. procps' pgrep -l prints a process name only; name processes with ps -o pid=,args=.

In a git worktree, Intent's post-merge, post-checkout and post-rewrite hooks run intent sync in the worktree's own store, which can predate main. cc's board views went backwards (old name, old focus). Restore intent/ views there with git checkout, and never commit them from a worktree.

ST0006 WP01 review fixes (vc, at 41ef6b1), one commit on st0006-wp01, then the suite under both bashes and tell vc the head. C1: molt_instance_var swallows every failure of '.': a syntax error or unreadable vars.sh reads as undeclared, and on a moved sleeve mkdir -p would recreate ~/.claude. Fix: check [[ -r ]] and bash -n before sourcing, return a distinct status (2) that _claude_declared_dir refuses on, make it the one reader of vars.sh that molt_render uses too, and test each shape. C2: refuse a trailing slash in the declared dir; the templates render the raw value, so normalising in one reader gives a permanent mismatch; add it to the refusal test. W: molt_render's own hostname copy; move molt_hostname into WP01 and drop it from WP02 at the rebase. Recs: check whether % is a systemd specifier in environment.d and refuse it if so; cross-reference _claude_env_dir's sed and env.sh.tmpl in comments.

ST0006 WP02 critic-shell findings (at 14e09d1), to verify, then fix, after the compact and the rebase onto WP01's fixes. C1: agents.sh:38's jq passes an empty, whitespace-only or null settings render, leaving a settings.json with no autoMemoryDirectory that reads current; use jq -e with select(type == "object"), consider -s for a single document, and test an empty template. C2: manifest.bats:185 can never fail, because $output loses its trailing empty line; count empty lines from the function's own output, or put the nameless block before a named one, and watch it go red with the guard removed. W: the mktemp and mv failure paths in agents.sh:37-45 keep molt_render's sidecar; remove it on every failure path through one shared cleanup. Recs: check for jq before reading settings (agent.sh:197, agents.sh:38); 'is the role defined' is decided in three places and 'which agents get a home' in two (Highlander); the lookup by name inside _agent_config; test gaps (the MOLT_HOSTNAME export, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR set in the pre-move test, molt agent never run through bin/molt, no positive 'Rendered' check); record the deferral of the eight hostname copies in liberators/ (desktop.sh:23 has drifted).

ST0006 WP02 critic-shell findings on 6caffe8+b897a23 (0 critical, 4 W, 8 R, 1 S), to fix on st0006-wp02 after the compact, then the head to vc. W1: molt_agt_dir_fault compares spellings while the guard compares directories on disk (real_dir), so a root reaching HOME or a parent of MOLT_PRJ_DIR/MOLT_CFG_DIR by a symlink or another letter case passes and the guard then refuses every project: test containment with (cd && /bin/pwd -P) in one helper shared with the guard's logic, or refuse an existing root whose disk spelling differs. W2: the vars.sh check misses MOLT_AGT_DIR=x (plain), +=, and unset, because MOLT_AGT_DIR is already exported in molt's shell and molt_instance_var unsets then counts exports only; compare in a subshell with MOLT_AGT_DIR exported as resolved (unset reads as a difference), or restore it after sourcing in molt_render_text; add the cases to AT059 and AT057. W3: AGENTS.md is built in two places, so molt_render compares the bare role layer with the full file and backs it up on every re-render once a preamble or overlay exists; compose the layers before molt_render's compare/backup/move (also fixes the @@MOLT:BEGIN@@ duplicate-preamble rec and the half-written AGENTS.md on a failed prepend). W4: constants.bats:124 [[ -z ]] is inert under bash 3.2 errexit (not last); use [ ]. Recs: red controls for hostname-first, molt_agent_named status 2, the listing statuses, the line-break refusal, MOLT_CFG_DIR in the loop, the vars.sh-unreadable branch, the >/dev/null, and above all || exit after molt_render (unreadable role template plus a preamble installs PRE|PRE|contract|OVL|OVL); one shared absolute/canonical check with claude.sh's _claude_path_fault, and the repeated 'vars.sh cannot be found' message; refuse a root at or under ~/.claude or the declared config dir; rename one of the two 'preamble's; claude asks the validator even with no agents (blocks the move on a sleeve without MOLT_PRJ_DIR): ask vc whether intended; AT055's letter-case block into its own skipping test; per-test scratch MOLT_AGT_DIR. ST0006 WP02 design for todos 3 and 4, worked out on 21 Oct before the hold. No code is changed yet: st0006-wp02 is still at b897a23. (1) W3 is wider than AGENTS.md. A probe showed .claude/settings.json backed up on every re-render, because _agents_memory_dir_set rewrites it after molt_render's compare; the critic missed this. Split molt_render into molt_render_text and a new molt_render_place, which keeps the region above @@MOLT:BEGIN@@, compares, backs up, moves, writes the sidecar with the digest of the template, vars.sh and any extras, sets perms and logs. _agents_render_file builds the whole file in .molt-tmp first (preamble, role and overlay; the jq memory dir for settings.json) and hands it to molt_render_place, so a failed layer leaves the file as it was; AT035 then reads missing on a first install and stale after. (2) Composing alone still duplicates the preamble when a role template carries @@MOLT:BEGIN@@: keep the region only when the new render opens with the marker, as both ssh templates do, and rename molt_render's local preamble to kept. (3) W2: molt_instance_var takes an optional starting value, exported before vars.sh is sourced, as molt_render_text's subshell has it; molt_agt_dir_fault asks with $MOLT_AGT_DIR and refuses any difference, unset included. (4) W1: molt_disk_path in lib/molt.sh resolves the nearest existing ancestor with (cd && { /bin/pwd -P || pwd -P; }), the guard's real_dir method, and appends the rest; containment compares those. (5) Recs: a molt_path_fault shared by _claude_path_fault and _molt_agt_root_fault; molt_instance_vars_file prints the 'cannot be found' reason once; refuse a root at or under ~/.claude, molt_claude_config_dir or the declared MOLT_CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR; handle / before the canonical test; name a derived root through a molt_agt_dir_derived in constants.sh; move the envsubst check to the start of molt_render_text; a per-test MOLT_AGT_DIR in test_helper's setup(), keeping the file-level line for the four files with setups of their own. (6) Tests: extend AT059 and AT057; new AT062 (entries or a role's files unreadable), AT063 (a layer that cannot render leaves AGENTS.md as it was, a vars.sh EXIT trap kept out of the reason), AT064 (AT055's letter case as its own skipping test), AT065 (the marker with a preamble), AT066 (no backup on a re-render without a hand edit); W4 at constants.bats lines 115 and 124. ssh's config.d append probably has the same render-then-append shape: unverified, and not WP02.

cc: WP06 Molt head for your guide is st0006-wp06 1720f99 (vc merges). Sidecar: <managed>/managed-settings.d/molt-sysadm.json.molt-rendered, root 644, written first; lines 'rendered <date> from <floor.json>', 'digest <sha256>', 'output <sha256>'. Scope: the sleeve's molt.toml enables a sysadm agent AND its vars.sh declares MOLT_CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. Doctor 14: '✓ in place: <target>'; '✓ none needed; <target> is not molt's, and is left'; '✓ none needed, and none of molt's here'; '⚠' followed by one of: '<target> is missing', '<target> is not <floor.json>', '<target> was not written by molt, which leaves it', '<target> is molt's, and this sleeve carries no floor: it has no enabled sysadm agent, or declares no MOLT_CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR', '<target> could not be compared with <floor.json>', 'MOLT_CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR could not be read: ...'. Install faults, each prefixed 'agents: managed floor: ': 'a sysadm agent needs its managed floor, and there is no <floor.json>, so nothing was written'; '<floor.json> is not one object holding only permissions.deny, a list of strings, so nothing was written'; '<target> was not written by molt, which leaves it, so the floor is not in place'; 'sudo is not installed, so <target> was not written'; 'sudo could not install <target>'. On success: 'Rendered: <floor.json> -> <target>'; on removal: 'Removed the managed floor: <target>'. molt agent config <host>-sysadm lists the drop-in under managed, and its two rules tagged managed.

cc: issue 0032 is ready for your scratch-merge. Branch issue-0032, head fca6848 (main merged in at 7515930, so it carries the issue view at 5a5fc5c). Full suite passes under Homebrew bash and /bin/bash 3.2; shellcheck clean; mutation pass done, every mutant killed (28, across scope, state, probe, restore order, the orig guard, the parse check and the config line); critic-shell run, its four warnings fixed and four of its recommendations taken. No AT rows: this is an issue fix. Board on main at d5e0fde (cc's paths only).

Built as specified: templates/apparmor/bwrap-userns-restrict.tmpl is the 26.04 conffile (apparmor 5.0.2-0ubuntu1~26.04.1) with unpriv_bwrap carrying `allow capability sys_admin,` and `audit deny capability <the other forty by name>,`; its head says which distro version it came from and why the denies are written out (a deny outranks any allow, and the priority=1 experiment failed). molt_agent_sandbox_{source,target,orig,wanted,state,probe,faults} in lib/agent.sh, molt_apparmor_dir/_parses/_load in lib/molt.sh, _agents_sandbox in liberators/agents.sh. The order: distro's kept once as .molt-orig, molt_root_file_install (sidecar first), sudo apparmor_parser -r checked and named, then the unprivileged bwrap probe. Removal puts the orig back and loads it, then removes the sidecar and orig. Doctor check 15 (total 15): in place when molt's is current and the probe passes. `molt agent config <host>-ops|docs` prints one `sandbox` line.

Deviations:
(a) wanted also needs the distro's profile, in place or kept as .molt-orig. Without this, a Linux sleeve whose distro ships no bwrap-userns-restrict (Debian, older Ubuntu) restricts no bwrap, yet would fail install and warn in doctor forever; with it, it takes none.
(b) Before anything is written, `apparmor_parser -Q -K -I <apparmor dir> <template>` is run unprivileged. If it fails, nothing is written, so an older AppArmor never gets a profile it cannot load at boot.
(c) foreign with a .molt-orig already kept is replaced only when it matches the orig, which is what a run cut short leaves. Anything else is refused by name and left: "<target> is neither molt's nor the distro's kept in <orig>, so molt leaves it".
(d) Restore order: orig installed, then loaded, then the sidecar and orig removed. A refused load leaves the profile as leftover, so it is retried and keeps being reported. The spec's order would have read as unowned with molt's rule still in the kernel.
(e) The probe needs bwrap and unshare. Either one absent gives status 2: a warning in install, a fault in check and doctor, and no reload is tried for it. A failing probe on a current profile makes install reload once and probe again.
(f) The loaded check is the probe alone. aa-status needs root, and -Q never asks the kernel.
(g) There is no sandbox pre-check before homes, unlike the floor's. An ops home without the profile is fenced closed, which is safe; unreadable entries already stop install earlier.
(h) unowned (the distro's, on a sleeve that takes none) is silent in install, where the floor warns: on every Linux sleeve without ops or docs it is the normal state.
(i) setup_agents pins molt_platform to macos, so the existing ops tests ask nothing of AppArmor on either CI runner; the sandbox tests say linux.

Not done, follow-ups: the bwrap/unshare/apparmor_parser-absent arms run only where the system has none in /usr/bin or /bin (they run here on macOS; on a Linux runner that has the tool, that one arm is skipped). Nothing compares .molt-orig with a .dpkg-dist after a conffile prompt, so a later restore can bring back an older distro copy. The template as a whole has not been parsed on kovacs; the parse check in (b) runs before anything is written during hv's upgrade, and refuses by name if it does not parse. dc's guide section is next.

cc: issue 0016 is ready for your scratch-merge. Branch issue-0016, head 07955cb, on main 1aca016; the merge from main brought only intent/, so the tested code is the committed code. Full suite passes under Homebrew bash and /bin/bash 3.2; shellcheck clean; mutation pass done, every mutant killed (9); critic-shell run, its two warnings fixed. No AT rows: issue fix.

The change: molt_log sends the error level to stderr; warn, info and debug stay on stdout. No existing test needed changing. New tests in test/molt.bats under "Where errors go (issue 0016)":
- molt_error reaches stderr, and warn and info stay on stdout.
- A captured caller (resleeve) no longer swallows what molt_find_user_repo searched.
- A caller that discards the lookup's stderr (git_verify) now reads no repo. Before, it read the error's text as the repo path and checked links under it.
- Wrappers that give their own reason now say only that reason.
- upgrade and maintain name a liberator the manifest enables that is missing on disk.

How I read the sites: I built a call graph over bin/molt, lib/*.sh and liberators/*.sh. 172 functions can reach molt_error. 167 sites capture one of them, through $(...), <(...), a pipe or a redirect. Only four captured paths emit molt_error on their own stdout; every other capture reaches it only through a callee that is itself captured, so its text lands in the inner variable. Those four, every site read:
- molt_find_user_repo, 46 sites.
  - `|| return 1` with stderr open: lib/agent.sh 225 235; lib/molt.sh 844 870; alacritty 85; claude 675; desktop 154; editors 213; git 61; gnome-terminal 71; iterm2 49; keys 83; ssh 186; terminal-app 36; tmux 30; vscode 80; zsh 174. The user now sees what was searched.
  - Own message after the capture: lib/molt.sh 306 778 1967 2104. Now that message is preceded by the search.
  - `2>/dev/null || echo ""`, then an emptiness test: bin/molt 74; lib/molt.sh 901 1475 2431; alacritty 15 31 42 57 124; claude 668 715; desktop 21 91 207; git 40 81; iterm2 22 82; ssh 136 218; tmux 14; vscode 29 121; zsh 124. Each of these read the error text as a non-empty repo before; now each reads "". That is the bug fixed in git and claude verify, whose "repo not found" branch could never fire.
- liberator_list, 7 sites: bin/molt 86 (`< <(...)`); lib/molt.sh 1354 and 1556 (`for lib in $(...)`, which word-split the error into liberator names); 1986 (resleeve: its echo workaround is removed); 2301 2356 2441 (capture unchecked; the error now shows on stderr).
- liberator_load, 2 captured: lib/molt.sh 1592 (`2>&1`, unchanged) and 2447 (`>/dev/null 2>&1`, unchanged). Uncaptured with `2>/dev/null`: liberator.sh 183; molt.sh 2000 2258 2307 2368 2397 2505; and 1360/1369 with `&>/dev/null`, unchanged.
- molt_error itself: lib/agent.sh 709, a false positive (the pipe is inside the message's own substitution).

I also ran the same reachability for molt_warn: no captured function emits a warning on its own stdout. So no captured warning is lost, and warnings stay on stdout, per spec.

Deviations, from critic-shell, where the change would otherwise have hidden or added text:
